description: Crash injection rollback evidence — every transition point tested for file consistency

crash_points_tested.file_state_after_crash: original (unchanged, backup exists, candidate rendered but not written)
fully edited (atomic rename completed, post-verify not run)
fully edited (all steps complete, registry not yet updated)

comprehensive_recovery_test.description: For each crash point: reset file to original, remove backup+registry, crash at that point, then re-run without crash. Assert: re-run succeeds, file has namtor block, file has pam_unix fallback.

atomicity_guarantee: The atomic rename(2) on a same-filesystem temp file ensures the PAM file is either fully original or fully edited — never half-written. The temp file is created in the same directory as the target, fsynced before rename, and the parent directory is fsynced after rename.
backup_guarantee: Before any edit, the original file is copied to <file>.namtor.bak with a SHA-256 checksum sidecar. Both are fsynced. The backup is preserved across re-enables (upgrade path). If the file was externally edited since the backup (stock content differs), the operation is refused with StaleEdit.
registry_guarantee: The enabled-service registry is updated only after the PAM file edit is verified. A crash before registry update leaves the file edited but registry stale — the next enable re-runs and updates the registry (idempotent).
